title: Students quitting is costing you money
sources: UPenn: ~4% of MOOC sign-ups completed; MIT/Harvard edX: ~5%

teyro.app/teach and /teach/how-it-works: streaks, weekly leagues, see where learners stop and nudge in one tap, subscriptions (paid every month a learner stays), keep 70% (80% Founding), free to publish, no camera needed

lines.text: If you sell online courses, | *students quitting* is costing you money | every *single* month.
Most people never finish online courses. | In big studies, only about *one in twenty* did. | And a student who quits | never pays you *again.*
Now picture a course | people open *every day.*
Your lessons keep a *streak* alive, | so missing a day feels like *losing* something.
Your students race each other | in *weekly leagues.*
You see the exact lesson where people *stop,* | and nudge them back | in *one tap.*
And because learners *subscribe,* | you get paid again | every month they *keep learning.*
You keep *seventy percent* of every payment, | publishing is *free,* | and you don't even need a *camera.*
Go to teyro dot app slash *teach.*
